assessments.reasoning: The pinned krzyzanowskim/CryptoSwift root LICENSE returned a complete body with the supplied publisher digest. The first line supplies the contact address and the final line supplies the acknowledgment.

The pinned json/details/CryptoSwift.json declares the exact identifier CryptoSwift. Its decoded licenseText preserves the publisher wording through the final acknowledgment with the contact suffix omitted.
The pinned text/CryptoSwift.txt confirms the same copyright line without the email and the same wording through the final acknowledgment.
The SPDX repository API's annotated v3.29.0 tag object targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in both CryptoSwift SPDX source URLs.

challenge.method: Compared the entire pinned root LICENSE from its copyright line through its final acknowledgment with the decoded SPDX licenseText and standalone text. Checked the year range, both spellings of the author's name, the acknowledgment URL and the four restrictions. Removed only the copyright-line contact suffix to test for further differences.
challenge.results: The publisher copyright line adds a single angle-bracketed email address after the author's name. After that suffix is removed, the decoded text agrees with both SPDX representations through the final acknowledgment. The accented copyright surname and unaccented acknowledgment surname occur in the same places in all three texts.

limitations: The comparison covers the sampled root LICENSE edition. Other revisions and approval-day copy identity were unverified.
Legal equivalence, text reuse, installation and work-specific applicability are outside scope.
Integrity checks used the retained response ranges and reported digests. The tag is unsigned, and the policy commit and bundle digest were supplied inputs.
reasoning: The exact CryptoSwift identifier and both pinned SPDX representations are bound to v3.29.0. The contact address on the publisher copyright line is the sole substantive textual offset in the cited passage.
